title: Dhanush's 'Kara' Crosses ₹50 Crore Mark, But Flop Tag Stings
excerpt: The Tamil heist thriller hits a global milestone after 10 days, yet recovers barely a quarter of its reported ₹100 crore budget.
body:
Dhanush's 54th film 'Kara' crossed ₹49–50 crore in worldwide box office collections after ten days in theatres, arriving at a milestone that offers cold comfort to its producers.

**What the numbers say:**
The Tamil heist drama, directed by Vignesh Raja, completed seven days in cinemas on May 6 after releasing globally on April 30, 2026. By the end of its first week, 'Kara' collected an estimated ₹47.49 crore worldwide, with ₹37.37 crore from domestic markets and ₹10.12 crore from overseas territories. It has since climbed to nearly ₹49.28 crore, approaching the ₹50 crore milestone. One bright spot is the international market — in its first four days alone, 'Kara' earned ₹9.15 crore overseas, nearly doubling what 'Idli Kadai' collected in the same window.

**Why the milestone does not mean much:**
'Kara' has been declared a flop, given its reported budget above ₹80–100 crore; even at ₹50 crore worldwide, the film has recovered only approximately 23–25% of its total investment. For a film of this scale to be a genuine hit, it would need to gross closer to ₹200 crore in India alone. 'Kara' is a Tamil-language heist and action thriller directed by Vignesh Raja, starring Dhanush in the titular role alongside Mamitha Baiju, and follows a reformed thief forced back into crime after his family's ancestral land is seized by a bank.

**What to watch:**
With 'Kara' currently tracking lower than Dhanush's previous films, its path to even partial budget recovery grows more challenging with each passing day — making OTT rights and satellite deals the next critical lifeline for its producers.
